item.title: 450 cartons of bottled water collected for drought-affected communities
item.description: A total of 450 cartons of bottled water have been collected through the Fiji Drought One Drop Bottle Water Appeal. The appeal has been organised by Sawani resident Sandeep Prakash, who is calling on members of the public to donate at least one bottle or carton of water to help families affected by the drought.
item.content:encoded:
A total of 450 cartons of bottled water have been collected through the Fiji Drought One Drop Bottle Water Appeal.

The appeal has been organised by Sawani resident Sandeep Prakash, who is calling on members of the public to donate at least one bottle or carton of water to help families affected by the drought.

He says, with the water collected so far, he will begin delivering supplies to affected communities in the Western Division on Monday.

Prakash says distribution will begin in the Tavua area, working with Advisory Councillor Hirdesh Nand to reach families who do not have Water Authority of Fiji meters.

He says the team then plans to continue to Ba, visiting communities in Moto Hill, Vatsui, Nukuloa, Tabataba and Waiwai.

Prakash has thanked people in Fiji and overseas who have contributed to the appeal, saying their generosity will help provide drinking water to families in need.

Members of the public who wish to donate bottled water can drop it off at his residence in Sawani, Nausori, beside the Royal Event Centre, at any time.

Those wishing to assist can also contact Prakash on 8610909.

item.title: Boy, 3, dies after being struck by vehicle at NSW holiday park
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 21/11/2026 A three-year-old boy has passed away after being hit by a small utility vehicle at a holiday park on the New South Wales Central Coast in Australia.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 21/11/2026

A three-year-old boy has passed away after being hit by a small utility vehicle at a holiday park on the New South Wales Central Coast in Australia.

Emergency services were called to the Blue Lagoon Beach Resort on Bateau Bay Road yesterday evening , following reports that a child had been hit by a vehicle.

Paramedics attempted to treat the toddler at the scene, but he could not be revived.

The driver of the Mitsubishi Triton, a 47-year-old man, was arrested and taken to hospital for mandatory testing.

A crime scene was established and examined by specialist officers.

Police say the driver was not related to the boy.

Preliminary evidence suggests the ute was travelling at a low speed, but investigations are ongoing.

item.title: People have lost trust in the Constitution Bill process – Prof. Prasad
item.description: The majority of people in Fiji have lost trust in the process being followed for the Constitution Amendment Bill. National Federation Party Leader Professor Biman Â Prasad highlighted this during fijivillage Straight Talk with Vijay Narayan when asked why the NFP is not supporting the third reading of the Bill.
item.content:encoded:
The majority of people in Fiji have lost trust in the process being followed for the Constitution Amendment Bill.

National Federation Party Leader Professor Biman Â Prasad highlighted this during fijivillage Straight Talk with Vijay Narayan when asked why the NFP is not supporting the third reading of the Bill.

He says the NFP cannot support the process, the implementation of the proposed constitutional changes or the third reading of the Bill because the party believes people have lost trust, and it cannot betray them.

He makes it clear that being part of a coalition government does not prevent individual parties from taking different positions on important national issues.

The NFP Leader says the party publicly identified 18 issues in the Cabinet Subcommittee's draft bill that needed attention.

He says the problems began with the draft bill itself, including errors, the proposal to recognise Christianity as a founding value and departures from the Constitution Review Commission's draft.

Professor Prasad says these issues created alarm and concern among the people.

He further says that although consultations were held, there was insufficient interaction with the public and little opportunity to properly explain many of the proposed provisions.

Professor Prasad says constitutional changes must have legitimacy and acceptance from the people, but he believes there is not enough time to achieve this.

Professor Prasad adds that the process should be left until after the next general election, while the Government focuses on more pressing issues.

Meanwhile, Deputy Party Leader Lenora Qereqeretabua says the 2013 Constitution was imposed on the people, and Fijians do not want another imposed constitution.

Qereqeretabua questioned the urgency of the proposed amendments, saying the process should be delayed until after the elections.

She says there are many more important priorities that need to be addressed, including drought, with people having to choose between providing water for their animals and other essential needs.

She adds that boreholes which were promised have yet to be dug.

The Deputy Party Leader says Fiji is also approaching the cyclone season, and she questioned if the country is prepared.

Qereqeretabua says there needs to be a much deeper conversation about the proposed amendments, and the first step should be to translate the Constitution Amendment Bill into languages that everyone can understand.

She adds that the consultation process has been conducted in English, with insufficient time given to submitters to express their views and concerns.
